attempted_claim: Let A,B be unital separable simple nuclear Z-stable C*-algebras. Suppose there exist an invertible element kappa in KK(A,B) with kappa_0([1_A])=[1_B], and an affine homeomorphism gamma: T(B)->T(A), compatible on the trace-K_0 pairing: <gamma(tau),x> = <tau,kappa_0(x)> for all tau in T(B), x in K_0(A). Does it follow that A is isomorphic to B? In particular, is this true without assuming (kappa,gamma) is induced by a unital *-homomorphism A->B and without assuming the UCT for A,B? If the stated pairing compatibility is insufficient, what is the minimal corrected KK-trace compatibility that implies A is isomorphic to B?
decisive_failure: originality: The strongest proved headline is already recorded and substantively implied: DRAFT Theorem 4/Corollary 6 is literally Schafhauser arXiv:2408.02745 Theorem A/Theorem 3.2 and Corollary B (one-sided embedding with invertible KK/KL plus invertible traces implies isomorphism; homotopy rigidity under projections-separate-traces). Theorems 2-3 are mechanical applications of the established UCT Elliott classification and Kirchberg-Phillips. Conjecture D as posed, the warning it may be too naive, the need for homomorphism-induced compatibility, and the AF sharpness example all appear in the same prior paper body. Full-text theorem-scope inspection gives COVERS_CLAIM; nothing new beyond restatement and gap commentary. value: No independently retrievable new fact under STANDARD: (a)-(b) are textbook corollaries of known classification theorems; (c) republication of Schafhauser Theorem A adds no new theorem, counterexample, census, cutoff, or exact invariant of a newly motivated object; (d) minimality/realizability commentary is interpretation of the known existence-vs-uniqueness gap, not a proved impossibility or a constructed witness. The core abstract stably-finite UCT-free question is left open by design (counterexample would imply non-UCT). Certification and faithful reproduction strengthen evidence but do not create value per STANDARD.
